v.why: Under Adam, wide layers make each fixed-size step change the output more, so raising LR overshoots there.
Three layers compound per-layer update magnitudes, so a higher LR destabilizes training more.
Tiny batches already give many noisy steps, so a bigger LR adds gradient-noise-driven instability.
sklearn divides the penalty by batch size, so small batches make the effective L2 much stronger and a further increase over-shrinks.
Narrow nets are capacity-limited, so extra shrinkage costs fit without a variance benefit.
A high LR with noisy small-batch gradients is unstable, so a larger batch averages the noise and stabilizes training.
The penalty is divided by batch size, so a larger batch weakens an otherwise over-strong L2 and reduces underfitting.
Extra width at an already large LR pushes the effective step past stability, since the optimal LR shrinks with width.
A one-hidden-layer net can only gain capacity through width, so width substitutes for missing depth.
Narrow nets lack capacity, and extra layers supply compositional capacity that width cannot.
